interventions.speaker: CHAIR
interventions.who: the senior urologist who signs the decision
interventions.body: The prognosis is influenced by several documented factors. The preoperative PSA was elevated at 7. The surgical findings include a pathological stage of pT3b, positive surgical margins, and invasion of the seminal vesicles, which are adverse prognostic indicators. Conversely, the absence of lymphovascular invasion is a favorable finding. The biopsy showed a lower grade (Gleason 3+4, ISUP grade group 2) compared to the prostatectomy specimen (Gleason 4+3, ISUP grade group 3), which may suggest a difference in tumor biology. The absence of lymph node removal (pNx) widens uncertainty regarding nodal status. The primary uncertainty lies in the missing postoperative PSA and follow-up data, which would significantly revise the trajectory of recurrence risk. The fixed estimated horizon is 38.79 months. This represents expected follow-up without an event, not a known recurrence date. The sensitivity range is 23.27–54.31 months; its coverage has not been validated.
